Join the Cato Institute for a conference with leading experts on the carrots and sticks of US policy and whether they will remain effective at an acceptable cost to Americans. 

🗓️ June 24, 10:00 a.m. – 2:05 p.m. EDT 
📍 Cato Institute, Washington, DC

That same standard, applied consistently, also condemns tariffs and US minimum taxes, writes Cato's @adamnmichel.

CBDCs aren't just a digital form of money. They're programmable, meaning the government can decide not only how much you have but what you're permitted to do with it. When money becomes a tool to permit or deny, financial autonomy and true liberty disappear, writes Cato’s @norbertjmichel.

The history of American technology policy is clear: light-touch regulation works best.

Financial surveillance is worsening as inflation, geographic targeting orders, and executive orders have expanded the scope of the Bank Secrecy Act. Congress has the power to fix it. 

Cato's @EconWithNick outlines the options: indexing reporting thresholds to inflation, strengthening the Right to Financial Privacy Act, and ending the Bank Secrecy Act.
